messages:
anya: quick sync — spike suggestion: ephemeral per-region private endpoints that mint short-lived tokens for a tokenized relay path. idea is to avoid long-lived peering and keep control plane out of customer VPCs.

mike: curious, how are we thinking about DNS+certs for that?

anya: tokens reference tenant+region+capabilities, signed by our controlplane KMS. relay validates token, does mutual TLS to our cp, and terminates to internal service. certs rotate per-ephemeral endpoint.

raj: sounds similar to pre-signed URL pattern but for networking. main worry: egress IP mapping for customer firewall rules — customers expect stable IPs sometimes.

anya: agreed. proposal: two modes — ephemeral (short-lived, for dev/low-compliance) and stable-affinity (allocates sticky egress IP pool per-customer in region). choose by tenant flag.

sofia: (minor) spelling: s/sofIa/sophia. Also how do we handle routing when relay capacity in region is saturated? fallback to cross-region with latency annotations?

mike: fallback yes, but need cost/latency policy. We could prefer same-region + burst cross-region. Also add a circuit-breaker that flips to customer-side NAT if they enabled peering earlier.

anya: circuit-breaker idea: automatically degrade from tokenized relay -> peered path -> customer-nat (if customer opted) based on SLOs. but that requires us to keep peering metadata around even if not primary.

raj: operational concern: debugging customer traffic becomes harder if endpoints are ephemeral. Need observability hooks: token metadata in flow logs, sampled request IDs, and a transparent header propagated to backend.

anya: yep — plan: relay injects x-rw-token-id and preserves original src ip in X-Forwarded-For for tracing. logs write token metadata to our tracing backend.

infra-bot: deploy-check: ephemeral-relay-proto v1 passed unit tests, integration queued for staging (PR #4128). :white_check_mark:

mike: security question — if token leaks, attacker could open a relay path for short window. mitigations?

anya: mitigations: 1) tokens have 1-5 minute TTL, 2) bound to source enclave (client cert) and tenant id, 3) rate limits and anomaly detection at relay.

raj: edge-case: customer on prem with strict egress policies — ephemeral IPs will break them. For those we force stable-affinity or require explicit peering.

anya: yep, plan to document: 3 onboarding tiers: 1) self-serve ephemeral (dev), 2) stable-affinity (prod w/ firewall rules), 3) peering/direct (regulated).

sofía: (lol) documented. also add a checklist for private CP: KMS access, route table guidance, and how to opt into stable pools.

mike: next steps: write RFC spike with sequence diagram, failure modes, and staging runbook. i'll volunteer to sketch diagrams.

anya: thanks — i'll draft RFC and include proto logs from infra-bot integration. tagging @raj for ops review and @sophia for onboarding docs.

raj: acked, will review latency/cost modeling.

sophia: will draft onboarding checklist after RFC.

anya: leaving this thread summary in #architecture for visibility. :+1:
